simple.meaning: חֵמָר (chêmâr) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “bitumen (as rising to the surface).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Genesis, Exodus, beginning at Genesis 11:3. Its contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֵמָר (H2564).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חֵמָר (chêmâr) / H2564 is traced through Genesis 11:3, Genesis 14:10, Exodus 2:3 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H2564. chemar חֵמָר noun [masculine] bitumen, asphalt (from I. חמר according to OBlau ZMG 1869, 279, bitumen as seething, swelling up ; Thes MV, from IV. חמר , with reference to reddish-brown colour) — חֵמָר Gen 11:3 2 t.; used for cement in building Babel 11:3 (J); abounding in vale of Siddim ח בֶּאֱרֹת ׳בֶּאֱרֹת 14:10 ; used in coating Moses' 'ark' of bulrushes Exod 2:3 (E; || זָ֑פֶת ).

occurrences.englishText: They said to one another, “Come, let’s make bricks, and burn them thoroughly.” They had brick for stone, and they used tar for mortar.
Now the valley of Siddim was full of tar pits; and the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, and some fell there. Those who remained fled to the hills.
When she could no longer hide him, she took a papyrus basket for him, and coated it with tar and with pitch. She put the child in it, and laid it in the reeds by the river’s bank.
